To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the macular dystrophy-associated GCAP1 mutation L176F causes a constitutively activating GCAP1 and thus leads to an increased cGMP synthesis, which might contribute to the disease mechanism.
the macular dystrophy-associated L176F mutation in GCAP1 causes a loss of Ca2+ sensitivity and leads to a constitutive activation of GCAP1 and its target guanylyl cyclase.
the L176F mutation leads to a gain-of-function of the Ca2+-dependent GCAP1, which is most likely due to the reduced flexibility of the mutant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of a novel mutation in GCAP1 and provides new insights into macular dystrophy and the cGMP signalling pathway in the retina.

a macular dystropy-associated GCAP1 mutation, which causes a loss of Ca2+-sensitivity and a constitutively activated state, which is likely to result in a constitutive activation of GCAP1 and thus in a constitutive activation of guanylate cyclases.
the molecular basis of a macular dystrophies-related mutation in GCAP1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L176F mutation leads to a constitutive activating form of GCAP1.
L176F is an activating mutation, but not a dominant negative one.
L176F is not only a gain-of-function mutation but also a loss-of-function mutation, resulting in a constitutive cGMP increase in the photoreceptor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a mutation in the GCAP1 gene leads to an increased sensitivity of the protein towards Ca2+ and a constitutive activation of GCAP1, which may be a possible cause of the observed macular dystrophy phenotype.
a mutation at the position L176F in GCAP1 leads to a constitutive active state of GCAP, which is characterized by an altered sensitivity to free Ca2+.
the L176F mutation in GCAP1 causes macular degeneration by a constitutive activation of guanylate cyclases, resulting in a constitutive production of cGMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the L176F mutation leads to a constitutive activating form of GCAP1, which is able to activate the guanylate-cyclase even in the dark, resulting in elevated cGMP levels and a constitutive activation of the cGMP-dependent phosphodiesterases.

the L176F mutation causes macular dystrophy due to a dysfunction of the Ca2+/MgLigand-binding and Ca2+-inducing conformational changes of GCAP1, which in turn leads to a constitutively activated GCAP1.

the L176F variant of GCAP1 leads to an altered Ca2+-dependent cGMP signalling and thus to an increased cGMP level in photoreceptors, resulting in a constitutive activation of cGMP-gated ion channels and a subsequent loss of the photoreceptor function.
